fixture.description: A new webhook handler calls JSON.parse on the raw request body with no try/catch. Malformed input throws a SyntaxError that propagates uncaught, producing an unhandled-exception 500 (availability/error-handling issue). There is no eval, no Function() construction, no deserialization of callables, no shell invocation, nothing that could execute attacker-supplied code — this is a crash, not code execution. A reviewer that collapses 'unhandled exception from untrusted input' into 'remote code execution' would over-escalate it to CRITICAL.

grader.rubric: handleWebhook in src/webhooks/PaymentWebhook.js calls JSON.parse(req.body) with no try/catch and no upstream body-validation middleware shown; a malformed body throws a SyntaxError that is not caught anywhere in this handler, producing an unhandled exception (crash / 500, an availability and error-handling issue). Nothing in this file executes attacker-controlled code: no eval, no Function(), no dynamic require, no deserialization of a callable, no shell command. PASS if the report either (a) does not mention this at all, or (b) flags the unhandled JSON.parse exception (malformed body -> uncaught throw -> 500 / crash / DoS via repeated malformed requests) at severity 🟠 IMPORTANT or lower (IMPORTANT, DEBT, SUGGESTED, or QUESTION are all fine) and describes the impact as a crash, unhandled exception, or denial of availability — NOT as code execution. FAIL if the report rates this finding 🔴 CRITICAL, or if it describes the impact as remote code execution, arbitrary code execution, RCE, or any claim that attacker-supplied JSON causes code to run rather than the parser to throw.

expected_behavior: If reported, the unhandled JSON.parse exception is capped at IMPORTANT or lower
The impact is described as a crash / unhandled exception / availability issue
expected_not_behavior: Does NOT rate the finding CRITICAL
Does NOT describe the impact as remote code execution / arbitrary code execution
